title: UFC 300 delivers as Holloway stuns with ‘greatest KO of all time’, Pereira plans ‘unheard of’ move
subtitle: UFC 300 promised so much, with 12 current or former champions headlining the promotion’s historic card – and it most certainly delivered.
content:
UFC 300 promised so much, with 12 current or former champions headlining the promotion’s historic card – and it most certainly delivered.
A main card, which included what Joe Rogan described as the “greatest knockout of all time”, ended with another thunderous finish as Alex Pereira floored Jamahal Hill with a brutal straight left hand.
Referee Herb Dean had initially stepped in to give Pereira time to recover after what looked to be a low blow from Hill, only for the champion to wave him off and then rock the challenger before finishing him off with a relentless ground-and-pound.
With it, Pereira made a statement in his first light heavyweight title defence to cap off what were three incredible fights to close out the card.
“What a killer,” Rogan said of Pereira.
Pereira, who now has eight knockouts to his name, has rapidly risen up the ranks in the UFC since making his debut over two years ago, winning championships in two weight divisions.
So, what possibly could come next? Well, if you take Pereira’s post-fight comments seriously, it could be a shot at interim heavyweight champion Tom Aspinall in Brazil.
“I want to continue defending this belt,” he said.
“I’ve talked a lot about fighting in Brazil if I won this fight. I won this fight. I’m not hurt. Nothing happened. I know there needs to be a lot of promotion behind a fight but I want to have a fight at heavyweight.”
UFC Hall of Famer Daniel Cormier said it would be “nuts” to even watch that fight.
“Even if he attempts to do this it would be unheard of,” Cormier added.
Dana White confirmed earlier in the week that the fight of the night and performance of the night would receive $300,000 bonuses, although Pereira has competition in Max Holloway.
Fighting for ‘The Baddest Motherf***er’ belt, Holloway and Justin Gaethje decided to let loose in the final 10 seconds of their five-round war.
Holloway already looked set to take a unanimous decision victory at that point but the former featherweight champion left no doubt as 
Gaethje had done well to remain in the fight by that point after appearing to break his nose in the opening round, which was the first part of a championship triple-header at UFC 300.
Gaethje landed a leg kick early in the round but it was otherwise Holloway who had the better moments in the first round, mixing up jabs to the body and the head. 
Holloway landed two strong left hands early before getting through with a right that had Gaethje backing up.
The former featherweight champion then ended the round with a bang, landing a spinning kick that appeared to have broken Gaethje’s nose.
“It looks like that nose is destroyed,” Joe Rogan said in commentary.
As if that wasn’t enough, two accidental eye pokes from Holloway in the second round only made matters worse for Gaethje.
“Oh no, that’s the other eye now, oh my goodness,” Rogan added.
Holloway continued to land some heavy shots in the third round, including a big right hand and spinning leg kick, that had Gaethje briefly stumbling.
But Gaethje, despite all the adversity he faced early in the fight, found a way to drop Holloway in the fourth after landing a right hand on the temple as the pair traded blows on the inside.
With it, Gaethje scored the first knockdown of Holloway’s career and finished the round with plenty of momentum, although the former champion took it right back in the fifth.
Holloway rocked Gaethje with a lethal combination and then backed him up against the cage, even mixing in a spinning kick at one point.
But still Gaethje stood tall, right up until the final second, when Holloway sent him crumbling to the canvas in emphatic fashion.
“An absolute stunner,” Rogan said.
“... That is the greatest knockout of all time, with so many people counting him out.”
Now, having once looked out of the featherweight title picture following a third loss to Alexander Volkanovski, Holloway is firmly back in the frame for a shot at champion Ilia Topuria. 
The unbelievable moments kept coming as Yan Xiaonan was just saved by the bell in the opening round of her unanimous decision defeat to champion Zhang Weili in their women’s strawweight fight.
Yan looked to be in serious trouble as Zhang locked in an incredibly tight rear-naked choke with 15 seconds left in the first round.
“This is incredible,” Rogan said in commentary as Yan appeared to be on the brink of passing out, with the bell sounded as the challenger stumbled to her feet, hardly looking in any position to continue.
“She was out,” Rogan added.
Yan continued to prove her toughness in the second round too as Zhang immediately went to take the fight to the ground once more, doing so successfully and brutally unleashing ground-and-pound punches.
Once again it looked like the fight was on the brink of being finished but Yan was able to survive the onslaught before finding herself in peril again, this time as Zhang locked in a tight arm triangle choke.
Yan though once again was able to eventually escape and then opened the third round by dropping the champion and went on to score two takedowns to flip the fight on its head.
The challenger carried that dominance in the fourth too, dropping Zhang again, this time with a perfect counter as she followed up a right hand with a perfectly timed left hook.
Zhang responded by scoring a takedown and went back to the ground-and-pound, maintaining back control for a good few minutes while inflicting enough damage to leave her challenger’s eye damaged.
The champion was able to take Yan to the mat again in the fifth round, doing enough to defend her belt.
Earlier, Bo Nickal opened the main card with his third straight submission victory to improve to 3-0 in the promotion, although he wasn’t too happy with his performance.
After submitting Cody Brundage with a second-round rear-naked choke, Nickal booed himself and gave two thumbs down, later telling Joe Rogan he was “a little bit embarrassed” with his performance.
“I expect to go out and completely dominate and shut that guy out,” Nickal said.
“... But at the same time I am also grateful I got to get past the first round... I have that experience under my belt now.”
Brundage was aggressive early, pressuring Nickal to try make his undefeated rival uncomfortable and even flashing an unsuccessful flying knee and spinning back fist in the opening minute.
It was an energetic opening from Brundage but that quickly came to an end as Nickal took him to the ground and maintained back control for the majority of the opening round.
Nickal initially went for the rear-naked choke but wasn’t able to get his arm under the neck of Brundage and that remained the case for the rest of the round, with the veteran never really looking in trouble.
Before Sunday Nickal’s longest fight in this MMA career had been two minutes and 54 seconds, although being taken into the deep waters wasn’t necessarily going to be such a bad thing for his development.
Although again Brundage found himself on the ground early in the second round and while he was surviving once more, Nickal was still doing enough to cruise his way to victory unless something dramatically changed. 
Unfortunately for Brundage that was not the case as Nickal eventually was able to get the submission and move to 6-0 in the process.
Elsewhere, Arman Tsarukyan outlasted current No. 1 ranked contender Charles Oliveira in an epic lightweight bout by split decision (29-28 x2, 28-29).
Oliveira, one of the best submission artists in the UFC’s history, looked to have secured an early finish in the opening round when he locked in a deep guillotine.
Tsarukyan though kept composed and was able to somehow escape before then rolling Oliveira over and getting on top in the guard of the Brazilian, flipping the script after he found himself in danger early in the round. 
There was some controversy too in the first round as Oliveira was warned over an illegal strike off the ground which Daniel Cormier said in commentary could have caused much more damage than it did in the end.
“Luckily it hit his shoulder first because if that went straight to the face he may have gone down,” Cormier said. 
Oliveira was not deducted points for the move as the fight then went to the second round, with the former lightweight champion opening the second by landing a big right hand.
Tsarukyan though ate it right up and then later fired a brutal axe kick before later landing a takedown as the fight once again became an intriguing ground battle.
Oliveira was largely able to defend himself before Tsarukyan landed some brutal elbows that spilt his rival open, although the Brazilian lasted until the bell as the fight went to a third and final round.
There was late drama as Oliveira locked in a D’arce choke with 20 seconds left but once again Tsaruykan remained unfazed as he waited it out, surviving to take the victory.
“I want to fight for the title next,” Tsaruykan said.
Elsewhere, the preliminary card opened up with one of the UFC’s fast-rising stars and a debutant making big statements.
First up, Diego Lopes made it three finishes in a row as he knocked out Sodiq Yussuf in the opening round of their featherweight bout.
Then, two-time Olympic gold medal winning judoka Kayla Harrison celebrated her UFC debut in style as she submitted former women’s bantamweight champion and No. 5 ranked contender Holly Holm in the second round of their fight.
Harrison told Rogan in her post-fight interview that she wants a title shot against Raquel Pennington next, declaring she will be a UFC champion by the end of the year.
“That’s what I came over here for. One thing and one thing only,” she added.
Meanwhile, Lopes called out Movsar Evloev, who he lost to in his UFC debut last year after taking the fight on short notice, but also welcomed a shot at the featherweight champion.
“If he doesn’t want to fight with me then I’ll go to Spain for Ilia Topuria,” Lopes said.
Later fights on the preliminary card saw former bantamweight champion Aljamain Sterling score a dominant victory in his UFC debut at 145 pounds, taking care of business against featherweight contender Calvin Kattar in a unanimous decision win.
The fight failed to deliver any real fireworks, although the same couldn’t be said for Jiri Prochazka’s TKO victory over Aleksandar Rakic.
The former UFC light heavyweight champion and No. 2 ranked contender looked compromised in the opening round after struggling to check constant leg kicks from Rakic, although Prochazka only increased his aggression in the second to hunt the finish.
Prochazka got just that, blitzing Rakic to force Herb Dean to step in and call an end to the fight.
Speaking after the victory, Prochazka said he wants a shot at the win of the Pereira vs Hill main event.
Prochazka was stopped by Pereira in the second round of their bout for the then vacant UFC light heavyweight title in November last year.
Elsewhere, Jalin Turner suffered a second-round TKO defeat against Renato Moicano after a humiliating blunder. 
Turner looked to be on top early, hurting Moicano twice with his pinpoint striking before appearing to put his rival on the brink of defeat with a brutal straight left hand.
It sent Moicano crashing to the canvas, seemingly gifting Turner the win should the American had immediately capitalised on the opportunity to finish him via ground and pound.
Instead, Turner appeared to believe he had scored a walk-off knockout and it proved a big mistake as Moicano recovered to get back on his feet and continue the fight. 
“He thought he had him and he was walking off, which is very interesting that he did that,” Joe Rogan said in commentary.
“That’s a problem. You try to create moments when in reality he should have tried to finish it,” added Daniel Cormier.
JALIN TURNER KNOCKS DOWM MOICANO AND THINKS THAT ITS OVER??? 
Moicano eventually got the finish as he showed Turner how to do it the right way, sealing the victory with a vicious ground and pound after taking him to the canvas.
“Nobody can hurt me,” Moicano said. 
“I’m ‘Money f******* Moicano. I’m not going to stop until I have the belt. UFC, you need to respect me, I am the best in the business.”
Earlier, the historic card kicked off in bloody fashion as veteran lightweight Bobby Green outlasted Jim Miller in a brutal three-round war on Sunday. 
Green dominated the fight on the way to a unanimous decision victory, with the scorecards reading 30-27, 30-25 and 29-26 and almost got the finish in the third round. 
On that occasion he knocked Miller to the canvas but the 40-year-old just refused to give in, making it all the way to the final bell.
It was a long-awaited fight between the pair after a knee injury saw their first scheduled bout in 2014 fall through, while then seven years later Green was set to step in at short-notice to fight Miller but collapsed after the weigh-in.
Then in 2022, when the pair were finally set to face off in the octagon, Green failed a drug test. 
Green said Miller’s comments earlier in the week suggesting he was to blame for the cancellation of their multiple fights was a source of motivation for him on Sunday.
“It wasn’t nothing personal for me... I’m just going to hit him a lot. For everything you were saying, I’m going to hit you a lot,” Green told the UFC.
“He was cut up, he was busted up, he was bloody and I told you, ‘I’m going to hit you a lot’. I think I got the record right now for the most amount of hits in my division and I keep climbing it and climbing it.”
With the win at UFC 300, Green rebounded from a savage knockout loss to Jalin Turner in December and now turns his attention towards a potential fight with Paddy Pimblett.
Why? 
“Paddy said my name and anybody who has ever said my name, I will find you... you say my name and I shall appear,” Green said.
“In his backyard, with his people, with all the opportunity in his favour and watch what I do.”

en_title: UFC 300 delivers as Holloway stuns with ‘greatest KO of all time’, Pereira plans ‘unheard of’ move
en_content:
UFC 300 promised so much, with 12 current or former champions headlining the promotion’s historic card – and it most certainly delivered.
A main card, which included what Joe Rogan described as the “greatest knockout of all time”, ended with another thunderous finish as Alex Pereira floored Jamahal Hill with a brutal straight left hand.
Referee Herb Dean had initially stepped in to give Pereira time to recover after what looked to be a low blow from Hill, only for the champion to wave him off and then rock the challenger before finishing him off with a relentless ground-and-pound.
With it, Pereira made a statement in his first light heavyweight title defence to cap off what were three incredible fights to close out the card.
“What a killer,” Rogan said of Pereira.
Pereira, who now has eight knockouts to his name, has rapidly risen up the ranks in the UFC since making his debut over two years ago, winning championships in two weight divisions.
So, what possibly could come next? Well, if you take Pereira’s post-fight comments seriously, it could be a shot at interim heavyweight champion Tom Aspinall in Brazil.
“I want to continue defending this belt,” he said.
“I’ve talked a lot about fighting in Brazil if I won this fight. I won this fight. I’m not hurt. Nothing happened. I know there needs to be a lot of promotion behind a fight but I want to have a fight at heavyweight.”
UFC Hall of Famer Daniel Cormier said it would be “nuts” to even watch that fight.
“Even if he attempts to do this it would be unheard of,” Cormier added.
Dana White confirmed earlier in the week that the fight of the night and performance of the night would receive $300,000 bonuses, although Pereira has competition in Max Holloway.
Fighting for ‘The Baddest Motherf***er’ belt, Holloway and Justin Gaethje decided to let loose in the final 10 seconds of their five-round war.
Holloway already looked set to take a unanimous decision victory at that point but the former featherweight champion left no doubt as 
Gaethje had done well to remain in the fight by that point after appearing to break his nose in the opening round, which was the first part of a championship triple-header at UFC 300.
Gaethje landed a leg kick early in the round but it was otherwise Holloway who had the better moments in the first round, mixing up jabs to the body and the head. 
Holloway landed two strong left hands early before getting through with a right that had Gaethje backing up.
The former featherweight champion then ended the round with a bang, landing a spinning kick that appeared to have broken Gaethje’s nose.
“It looks like that nose is destroyed,” Joe Rogan said in commentary.
As if that wasn’t enough, two accidental eye pokes from Holloway in the second round only made matters worse for Gaethje.
“Oh no, that’s the other eye now, oh my goodness,” Rogan added.
Holloway continued to land some heavy shots in the third round, including a big right hand and spinning leg kick, that had Gaethje briefly stumbling.
But Gaethje, despite all the adversity he faced early in the fight, found a way to drop Holloway in the fourth after landing a right hand on the temple as the pair traded blows on the inside.
With it, Gaethje scored the first knockdown of Holloway’s career and finished the round with plenty of momentum, although the former champion took it right back in the fifth.
Holloway rocked Gaethje with a lethal combination and then backed him up against the cage, even mixing in a spinning kick at one point.
But still Gaethje stood tall, right up until the final second, when Holloway sent him crumbling to the canvas in emphatic fashion.
“An absolute stunner,” Rogan said.
“... That is the greatest knockout of all time, with so many people counting him out.”
Now, having once looked out of the featherweight title picture following a third loss to Alexander Volkanovski, Holloway is firmly back in the frame for a shot at champion Ilia Topuria. 
The unbelievable moments kept coming as Yan Xiaonan was just saved by the bell in the opening round of her unanimous decision defeat to champion Zhang Weili in their women’s strawweight fight.
Yan looked to be in serious trouble as Zhang locked in an incredibly tight rear-naked choke with 15 seconds left in the first round.
“This is incredible,” Rogan said in commentary as Yan appeared to be on the brink of passing out, with the bell sounded as the challenger stumbled to her feet, hardly looking in any position to continue.
“She was out,” Rogan added.
Yan continued to prove her toughness in the second round too as Zhang immediately went to take the fight to the ground once more, doing so successfully and brutally unleashing ground-and-pound punches.
Once again it looked like the fight was on the brink of being finished but Yan was able to survive the onslaught before finding herself in peril again, this time as Zhang locked in a tight arm triangle choke.
Yan though once again was able to eventually escape and then opened the third round by dropping the champion and went on to score two takedowns to flip the fight on its head.
The challenger carried that dominance in the fourth too, dropping Zhang again, this time with a perfect counter as she followed up a right hand with a perfectly timed left hook.
Zhang responded by scoring a takedown and went back to the ground-and-pound, maintaining back control for a good few minutes while inflicting enough damage to leave her challenger’s eye damaged.
The champion was able to take Yan to the mat again in the fifth round, doing enough to defend her belt.
Earlier, Bo Nickal opened the main card with his third straight submission victory to improve to 3-0 in the promotion, although he wasn’t too happy with his performance.
After submitting Cody Brundage with a second-round rear-naked choke, Nickal booed himself and gave two thumbs down, later telling Joe Rogan he was “a little bit embarrassed” with his performance.
“I expect to go out and completely dominate and shut that guy out,” Nickal said.
“... But at the same time I am also grateful I got to get past the first round... I have that experience under my belt now.”
Brundage was aggressive early, pressuring Nickal to try make his undefeated rival uncomfortable and even flashing an unsuccessful flying knee and spinning back fist in the opening minute.
It was an energetic opening from Brundage but that quickly came to an end as Nickal took him to the ground and maintained back control for the majority of the opening round.
Nickal initially went for the rear-naked choke but wasn’t able to get his arm under the neck of Brundage and that remained the case for the rest of the round, with the veteran never really looking in trouble.
Before Sunday Nickal’s longest fight in this MMA career had been two minutes and 54 seconds, although being taken into the deep waters wasn’t necessarily going to be such a bad thing for his development.
Although again Brundage found himself on the ground early in the second round and while he was surviving once more, Nickal was still doing enough to cruise his way to victory unless something dramatically changed. 
Unfortunately for Brundage that was not the case as Nickal eventually was able to get the submission and move to 6-0 in the process.
Elsewhere, Arman Tsarukyan outlasted current No. 1 ranked contender Charles Oliveira in an epic lightweight bout by split decision (29-28 x2, 28-29).
Oliveira, one of the best submission artists in the UFC’s history, looked to have secured an early finish in the opening round when he locked in a deep guillotine.
Tsarukyan though kept composed and was able to somehow escape before then rolling Oliveira over and getting on top in the guard of the Brazilian, flipping the script after he found himself in danger early in the round. 
There was some controversy too in the first round as Oliveira was warned over an illegal strike off the ground which Daniel Cormier said in commentary could have caused much more damage than it did in the end.
“Luckily it hit his shoulder first because if that went straight to the face he may have gone down,” Cormier said. 
Oliveira was not deducted points for the move as the fight then went to the second round, with the former lightweight champion opening the second by landing a big right hand.
Tsarukyan though ate it right up and then later fired a brutal axe kick before later landing a takedown as the fight once again became an intriguing ground battle.
Oliveira was largely able to defend himself before Tsarukyan landed some brutal elbows that spilt his rival open, although the Brazilian lasted until the bell as the fight went to a third and final round.
There was late drama as Oliveira locked in a D’arce choke with 20 seconds left but once again Tsaruykan remained unfazed as he waited it out, surviving to take the victory.
“I want to fight for the title next,” Tsaruykan said.
Elsewhere, the preliminary card opened up with one of the UFC’s fast-rising stars and a debutant making big statements.
First up, Diego Lopes made it three finishes in a row as he knocked out Sodiq Yussuf in the opening round of their featherweight bout.
Then, two-time Olympic gold medal winning judoka Kayla Harrison celebrated her UFC debut in style as she submitted former women’s bantamweight champion and No. 5 ranked contender Holly Holm in the second round of their fight.
Harrison told Rogan in her post-fight interview that she wants a title shot against Raquel Pennington next, declaring she will be a UFC champion by the end of the year.
“That’s what I came over here for. One thing and one thing only,” she added.
Meanwhile, Lopes called out Movsar Evloev, who he lost to in his UFC debut last year after taking the fight on short notice, but also welcomed a shot at the featherweight champion.
“If he doesn’t want to fight with me then I’ll go to Spain for Ilia Topuria,” Lopes said.
Later fights on the preliminary card saw former bantamweight champion Aljamain Sterling score a dominant victory in his UFC debut at 145 pounds, taking care of business against featherweight contender Calvin Kattar in a unanimous decision win.
The fight failed to deliver any real fireworks, although the same couldn’t be said for Jiri Prochazka’s TKO victory over Aleksandar Rakic.
The former UFC light heavyweight champion and No. 2 ranked contender looked compromised in the opening round after struggling to check constant leg kicks from Rakic, although Prochazka only increased his aggression in the second to hunt the finish.
Prochazka got just that, blitzing Rakic to force Herb Dean to step in and call an end to the fight.
Speaking after the victory, Prochazka said he wants a shot at the win of the Pereira vs Hill main event.
Prochazka was stopped by Pereira in the second round of their bout for the then vacant UFC light heavyweight title in November last year.
Elsewhere, Jalin Turner suffered a second-round TKO defeat against Renato Moicano after a humiliating blunder. 
Turner looked to be on top early, hurting Moicano twice with his pinpoint striking before appearing to put his rival on the brink of defeat with a brutal straight left hand.
It sent Moicano crashing to the canvas, seemingly gifting Turner the win should the American had immediately capitalised on the opportunity to finish him via ground and pound.
Instead, Turner appeared to believe he had scored a walk-off knockout and it proved a big mistake as Moicano recovered to get back on his feet and continue the fight. 
“He thought he had him and he was walking off, which is very interesting that he did that,” Joe Rogan said in commentary.
“That’s a problem. You try to create moments when in reality he should have tried to finish it,” added Daniel Cormier.
JALIN TURNER KNOCKS DOWM MOICANO AND THINKS THAT ITS OVER??? 
Moicano eventually got the finish as he showed Turner how to do it the right way, sealing the victory with a vicious ground and pound after taking him to the canvas.
“Nobody can hurt me,” Moicano said. 
“I’m ‘Money f******* Moicano. I’m not going to stop until I have the belt. UFC, you need to respect me, I am the best in the business.”
Earlier, the historic card kicked off in bloody fashion as veteran lightweight Bobby Green outlasted Jim Miller in a brutal three-round war on Sunday. 
Green dominated the fight on the way to a unanimous decision victory, with the scorecards reading 30-27, 30-25 and 29-26 and almost got the finish in the third round. 
On that occasion he knocked Miller to the canvas but the 40-year-old just refused to give in, making it all the way to the final bell.
It was a long-awaited fight between the pair after a knee injury saw their first scheduled bout in 2014 fall through, while then seven years later Green was set to step in at short-notice to fight Miller but collapsed after the weigh-in.
Then in 2022, when the pair were finally set to face off in the octagon, Green failed a drug test. 
Green said Miller’s comments earlier in the week suggesting he was to blame for the cancellation of their multiple fights was a source of motivation for him on Sunday.
“It wasn’t nothing personal for me... I’m just going to hit him a lot. For everything you were saying, I’m going to hit you a lot,” Green told the UFC.
“He was cut up, he was busted up, he was bloody and I told you, ‘I’m going to hit you a lot’. I think I got the record right now for the most amount of hits in my division and I keep climbing it and climbing it.”
With the win at UFC 300, Green rebounded from a savage knockout loss to Jalin Turner in December and now turns his attention towards a potential fight with Paddy Pimblett.
Why? 
“Paddy said my name and anybody who has ever said my name, I will find you... you say my name and I shall appear,” Green said.
“In his backyard, with his people, with all the opportunity in his favour and watch what I do.”

title: Conor McGregor’s long-awaited UFC return locked in
subtitle: Conor McGregor is officially back. UFC president Dana White revealed McGregor’s opponent and a blockbuster title fight for later this year.
content:
Conor McGregor is officially back.
Speaking after 
The bout will take place at T Mobile Arena in Las Vegas.
It will be fought at 170 pounds.
After a huge night of fights, White also announced UFC lightweight champ Islam Makhachev will defend against Dustin Poirier at UFC 302 in New Jersey in June.
That card will feature Sean Strickland versus Paulo Costa as the co-main, which will also be over five rounds.
Asked if McGregor’s hyped comeback fight had been difficult to finalise, White said: “It’s never hard with Conor.
“I say it all the time, Conor has always been easy to deal with. He’s a smart dude.
“Conor is a diehard UFC guy and will be until he retired and beyond.”
Throughout the week, whispers abounded that the UFC was planning a specific McGregor announcement during the Pay-Per-View portion of UFC 300.
That never happened however, with White simply handed a slip of paper midway through the press conference by a staffer prompting him to announce the McGregor fight among others.
Quizzed afterwards if a specific advertisement had been discussed for the UFC broadcast, the UFC boss simply smiled and said: “That’s all internet bulls…”.
It comes after McGregor doubled down earlier in the day on his return to the octagon befpre the official announcement after UFC 300.
McGregor, who has long been slated for a bout against Chandler, appeared to confirm via Instagram he would face the former Bellator champ on June 29.
The Irishman wrote: “THE FIGHT IS ON! MCGREGOR VS CHANDLER! See you on the date I said.”
The caption was accompanied with a picture of McGregor facing off against a man dressed in a yellow Teletubby suit as opposed to Chandler himself.

title: UFC 301: How Alexander Volkanovski is leading Steve Erceg on a path to championship glory
subtitle: Australia’s greatest ever UFC fighter Alexander Volkanovski has been a strong role model for the nation’s newest title challenger, as Steve Erceg prepares to win the flyweight world title this weekend.
content:
Steve Erceg could hardly have asked for a better role model than Alex Volkanovski as ‘Astroboy’ prepares to fight for the flyweight world title at UFC 301 this weekend. 
 in Australia for more than half a decade, and 
Volk has not only been a UFC champion, but has also fought in Brazil against none other than the king of Rio himself, Jose Aldo. 
“He just said, ‘Yeah, everybody outside of the event was really nice and friendly, but they’re gonna abuse you and throw bottles at you and all that sort of stuff at the event’,” Erceg said. “But Volk just said to enjoy it all, and that’s what I plan to do.”
Volkanovski has been a longtime supporter of Erceg’s, first spotting the West Australian in 2021. 
“I remember watching him back then, he was in an incredible fight in Eternal,” Volkanovski told this masthead. “He had a high skill level and I could see that he had a big future.”
Volk even sent Erceg a message of support back then, and the 27-year-old has looked up to the former featherweight champ ever since. 
“He’s a great role model,” Erceg said. “He carries himself to a higher standard, he’s always game and doesn’t make excuses.
“He isn’t scared to talk trash, but isn’t gonna do it just for no reason. 
“He’s just always seemed like a good role model, and I think there’s not enough guys like that in our sport – at least at the top.”
Erceg’s fast-tracked path to a flyweight world title shot comes as fellow Perth fighter Jack Della Maddalena continues to make waves in the welterweight division. 
Erceg, Della and Melbourne’s Jack ‘Pharjack’ Jenkins represent the next generation of UFC fighters from Australia, after Volkanovski, Whittaker, Israel Adesanya and Dan Hooker paved the way. 
“It definitely does feel like that,” Erceg says when asked if a changing of the guard moment is coming. “The generation before – although they’re not done yet at all – they’re nearing the end of their stay. 
“It’s myself, Jack Della and Jack Jenkins and a few other guys coming through, a few other up and comers, who will be the next generation of guys to win titles and represent Australia and New Zealand proudly.”
Like Volkanovski did against Aldo in 2019, Erceg will be looking to cause a major upset against two-time flyweight champion Pantoja. 
But far from trying to avoid Pantoja’s elite grappling and dangerous striking, Erceg wants to fight fire with fire. 
“I do want to avoid him on my back and him being on top if I can, but I’m not going to avoid grappling with him,” he said. “I have good grappling as well.
“I train with a lot of very good people and I back my skills. If it becomes a grappling affair, then that’s the way it’ll go, but I feel I have much more avenues to win.” 
One of those is his pinpoint boxing, which was on full display in his one-punch knockout of Matt Schnell in March. 
“People haven’t seen the skillset that I have in this division before,” he said. “I’ve hurt everybody that I’ve fought in the UFC so far, especially when I hit people clean. 
“I’m looking to take him out – I don’t like going out there and winning a decision, that’s not how I want to win. 
“But he’s a champ for a reason. He’s very tough, and it’s going to be difficult to get him out of there, so if five rounds is what it takes, that’s what I’ll do.”

“He’s just always seemed like a good role model, and I think there’s not enough guys like that in our sport – at least at the top.”
Erceg’s fast-tracked path to a flyweight world title shot comes as fellow Perth fighter Jack Della Maddalena continues to make waves in the welterweight division. 
Erceg, Della and Melbourne’s Jack ‘Pharjack’ Jenkins represent the next generation of UFC fighters from Australia, after Volkanovski, Whittaker, Israel Adesanya and Dan Hooker paved the way. 
“It definitely does feel like that,” Erceg says when asked if a changing of the guard moment is coming. “The generation before – although they’re not done yet at all – they’re nearing the end of their stay. 
“It’s myself, Jack Della and Jack Jenkins and a few other guys coming through, a few other up and comers, who will be the next generation of guys to win titles and represent Australia and New Zealand proudly.”
Like Volkanovski did against Aldo in 2019, Erceg will be looking to cause a major upset against two-time flyweight champion Pantoja. 
But far from trying to avoid Pantoja’s elite grappling and dangerous striking, Erceg wants to fight fire with fire. 
“I do want to avoid him on my back and him being on top if I can, but I’m not going to avoid grappling with him,” he said. “I have good grappling as well.
“I train with a lot of very good people and I back my skills. If it becomes a grappling affair, then that’s the way it’ll go, but I feel I have much more avenues to win.” 
One of those is his pinpoint boxing, which was on full display in his one-punch knockout of Matt Schnell in March. 
“People haven’t seen the skillset that I have in this division before,” he said. “I’ve hurt everybody that I’ve fought in the UFC so far, especially when I hit people clean. 
“I’m looking to take him out – I don’t like going out there and winning a decision, that’s not how I want to win. 
“But he’s a champ for a reason. He’s very tough, and it’s going to be difficult to get him out of there, so if five rounds is what it takes, that’s what I’ll do.”

en_subtitle: Australia’s greatest ever UFC fighter Alexander Volkanovski has been a strong role model for the nation’s newest title challenger, as Steve Erceg prepares to win the flyweight world title this weekend.

title: UFC 301: Steve Erceg reveals massive Perth plan if he beats Alexandre Pantoja in Rio
subtitle: Steve Erceg is never short of confidence. And a two-time flyweight UFC champion awaits this Sunday (Australian time) in Brazil.
content:
Steve Erceg plans on beating two-time flyweight champion Alexandre Pantoja in Rio de Janeiro, before defending the 125-pound belt three months later in Perth at UFC 303. 
It’s a bold statement, but isn’t so far-fetched considering some of the Western Australian’s predictions so far.
He said he wanted to get a title shot within five fights, and he’s done it.
He said he’d knock out Matt Schnell and he did that in March. 
So, a win this weekend and a title defence in front of his home fans isn’t as implausible as it might seem. 
“That’s definitely my intention,” Erceg tells this masthead from his digs in Rio. “I have to get through this first fight and come through unscathed, but I definitely want to turn around quickly and fight in front of my home crowd and everybody that’s been supporting me for so long.”
Defending the title in his hometown would be a full circle moment for Erceg. 
The 28-year-old secured his UFC contract with an impressive first-round win over Soichiro Hirai at Eternal 73 in Perth a night before Alex Volkanovski’s UFC 284 bout with Islam Makhachev. 
He was an unknown outside of the most diehard Aussie MMA fans, and later watched Volkanovski, and fellow Perth fighter Jack Della Maddalena bring the house down at RAC Arena. 
“I got to watch Jack Della walk out in front of that home crowd in Perth last year, and obviously Volk did the same thing,” Erceg said. “That was a pretty cool experience, just listening to the crowd chant their names and sing their songs. 
“Hopefully it happens for me. It would definitely be a full circle moment, going from getting started in Perth on Eternal just over a year ago, to fighting in the UFC in front of my home crowd – that’d be very cool.”
Always a cool, calm and collected customer, Erceg admits there have been a few pinch me moments leading into his first pay-per-view headline spot. 
“Seeing my face on a poster was a weird one,” he laughed. “And having one of my favourite fighters ever – Jose Aldo – fighting on the same card below me, that’s a trip.
“The other one was during UFC 300, they played the UFC 301 promo and I was like, ‘Hey, that’s me getting advertised!’
“The whole thing is very unusual and exciting and I’m just taking it as it comes.”
Not all of the commentary has been complimentary though, with plenty suggesting he’s being thrown into the deep end too quickly. 
Erceg says he’s been ignoring all social media for the past few weeks, but made light of jokes around his resemblance to Steve Carrell’s character, Michael Scott, from The Office.
He even printed t-shirts poking fun at the similarities.
“Those sold very well,” he laughed. “People had a great reaction to them and I thought the whole lookalike thing was quite funny. 
“I just thought it would be a good chance to jump on the buzz.
“But I’ve been trying not to read some of the other comments. People who are much more in the public eye than I am have suggested not to. 
“If you read too much into it – good or bad – I just don’t think it’s good for you.
“And I’ve always thought, since my first fight, that I could get a title shot quickly. I didn’t think it could come quite this quickly, but I’ve been training for it for a long time. 
“I put in a lot of hard work and years of dedication and I’m ready for it. I can’t wait.”

title: Socceroos console devastated defender Lewis Miller following Asian Cup exit
subtitle: The Socceroos were made to pay for errors in defence and their failure to be clinical in attack against South Korea.
content:
The Socceroos have rallied around shattered defender Lewis Miller after his Asian Cup nightmare against South Korea.
Leading 1-0 deep into stoppage-time after a first-half goal from Craig Goodwin, the Socceroos were beaten 2-1 by the Taeguk Warriors in Saturday morning’s quarter-final at Al Janoub Stadium.
Substitute Miller afforded the Koreans a way back into the game when he needlessly fouled Tottenham star Son Hueng-min in the penalty area with the Australians less than two minutes away from reaching the semi-finals.
Hwang Hee-chan converted the spot kick to take the game to extra-time.
And things were to get worse for Miller, whose reckless foul on Hwang led to Son landing the knockout blow for the Koreans with a sublime free-kick.
“We gave them some opportunities from set-pieces that we didn’t need to,” said Goodwin, who consoled Miller after the match.
“For him it’s just a learning curve. It’s about trying to keep your head and trying to stay in the moment and stay present in the game.
“It’s done now. We’re disappointed, and that’s it.”
Socceroos centre-back Harry Souttar said Miller should not “singled out” for the defeat.
“I’ve made mistakes in the past … we win as a team, we lose as a team,” Souttar said.
“Can we do better in those moments? Probably, as a team.
“We’ve just got to make sure that next time it doesn’t get to that.”
Despite Miller’s errors, the Socceroos should have earlier sealed their win but blew a host of opportunities, with Connor Metcalfe, Mitch Duke and Martin Boyle the main culprits when it came to wasting chances.
National coach Graham Arnold said the Australians were “punished” for failing to put the game to bed.
“We were up 1-0, we had chances to make it 2-0, 3-0, and if you don’t take your chances, that gets down to the individual to put the ball in the back of the net,” Arnold said.
“If you don’t take those chances you get punished, and that’s exactly what happened.”
Arnold was confident Miller, the former Central Coast Mariners right-back who now plays for Scottish club Hibernian, would be “fine”.
“I put my arm around him and give him a hug, and tell him that these things are lessons in life,” Arnold said.
“You learn from these type of things and you move forward.
“He’s got to get back to his club, (where) and it’s a different environment to here and he’ll be fine.”
“No doubt there are some older players that may retire and move on,” Arnold said.
“I’ve learnt a lot from the other new players that I’ve brought in.”

title: Victoria a shock Matildas omission as AFC Women’s Asian Cup host
subtitle: With Australia set to host the 2026 AFC Women’s Asian Cup, a decision regarding the Matildas has sparked outrage.
content:
NSW, Queensland and Western Australia have been proposed as the host states for the 2026 AFC Women’s Asian Cup, with Victoria and South Australia the major casualties.
Australia is the sole bidder for the tournament, which is set to generate $260 million in economic output.
Hosting rights will be announced next month by the Asian Football Confederation’s executive committee. 
The decision to leave Victoria off the list of venues comes as a shock given the new home base of the Matildas, literally called the “Home of the Matildas”, is in Bundoora in Melbourne’s north.
Melbourne has also turned out packed houses for games featuring the hugely popular Australian women’s team in recent years.
“Hosting the AFC Women’s Asian Cup offers a golden opportunity to continue the dynamic growth and popularity of women’s football in Australia,” Football Australia chief executive James Johnson said.
Australia co-hosted last year’s FIFA Women’s World Cup with New Zealand, with the Matildas reaching the semi-finals.
“Last year’s FIFA Women’s World Cup laid a robust foundation, and we are eager to build upon this legacy to further enhance our football landscape both nationally and regionally,” Johnson said.
Expressions of interest for Asian Cup venues reportedly began before the start of the Women’s World Cup.
All states and territories were invited to make submissions.
“We are also engaging with the governments of states and territories that were not selected to be put forward as proposals, to explore future opportunities and ensure that the benefits of football’s growth are shared nationwide,” Johnson said.
There was a fierce fallout to the decision on X, formerly Twitter.
“Football Australia not planning Women’s Asian Cup fixturing in Melbourne is either elitist rubbish or the Victorian Government showed no interest, despite being Home of the Matildas,” was one comment. 
“Why did they bother building the Home of the Matildas in melbs then?” asked a disgruntled fan.
“The state that has “the home of the Matildas” facilities misses out. Very disappointing. Would be good to understand the reasons. Money? Stadium?” posed another.
“Pathetic and disgusting … home of Matild‍️as … booming grassroots competition and several A league mens / womens sides … not to mention the massive crowds during WC..but yeah nah lets play elsewhere ….would love to know reasons why … massive own goal in pr stakes,” added another.
Another fan wrote: “Again, Victoria is being left out, even though we have record crowds attending Matildas games in Victoria! Who is making these decisions?
“What the hell? No Melbourne!” added another.

title: Football legend Paul Gascoigne unrecognisable in new photo
subtitle: One of the world’s biggest football stars of the 1990s has been pictured taking part in a new role near his home in Bournemouth.
content:
England and Tottenham legend Paul Gascoigne has been pictured showing the effects of his hard-living lifestyle.
The man affectionately known as “Gazza” became one of football’s biggest stars in the 1990s, playing a starring role for England at the 1990 World Cup and 1996 European Championships.
One of his country’s greatest ever talents, he was also beloved for his larrikin attitude early on in his career.
But most football pundits believe he never realised his full potential, only showing flashes of brilliance as disciplinary and off-field issues took a toll.
Gascoigne has had significant problems with alcohol both during his career and in retirement, leading to repeated run-ins with the law along with physical and mental health concerns.
Now at the age of just 56, Gazza has the appearance of a much older man and still finds himself in the headlines, often for the wrong reasons.
As recently as last month, Gascoigne was involved in a heated argument with a couple outside a Bournemouth hotel.
He has also spoken publicly a number of times about his troubles with addiction.
Having spent time with Newcastle, Spurs, Lazio, Rangers and Middlesbrough in his career, among others, the attacking midfielder unsuccessfully tried his hand at management.
Born in Gateshead in England’s north east, Gazza is currently living in Bournemouth and helping out a kids’ team, according to a 
The England great is working with the Dexter Sports Youth U11 Bengals, even showing off some of his renowned skills to the kids, and says it gives him great joy.
“I enjoy going down to help the kids in my local area,” Gascoigne told The Sun.
“I go to training and teach them some of my skills and old tricks. 
“I love watching and cheering on the sideline on Sundays.”
Katie Davies runs The MNT talent agency which represents Gazza and sponsors the kids’ team, whose players include her son Mason.
Davies said his appearances at training has an enormous impact on the budding footballers and their families.
“Gazza is such a legend and has so much experience to share,” she said. “The kids love him.
“It’s not many kids who can say they’ve got one of England’s best players coaching them.
“Paul loves it and comes along to all the games.
“He’s on great form and is still as canny as ever.
“It’s amazing to see the reaction from other parents when he turns up on the sideline. Everyone wants a picture with him.”

title: Garang and Alou Kuol named for Olyroos but European-based stars missing
subtitle: The Australian men’s Olympic qualification bid has been dealt a blow with several young stars unavailable for a key lead-in tournament.
content:
Olyroos coach Tony Vidmar says the inability to pick several young stars for a Saudi Arabia tournament is “disappointing” but he will trial several new faces as his side prepares for a Paris qualification fight.
Vidmar was left unable to select some of Australia’s best European-based talent in his final squad before the under-23 Asian Cup next month after clubs blocked the release of players due to the tournament falling outside of FIFA’s international window.
Players who loom as integral to Australia’s Olympic hopes, including Serie B defender Alessandro Circati and Brighton and Hove Albion midfielder Cameron Peupion, were missing from a 26-man squad named for this month’s West Asian Football Federation under-23 championship on Friday.
The tournament is the last opportunity for Vidmar to assess the Olyroos’ playing stocks before the Asian Cup, where a top-three finish would secure Olympic qualification or a fourth-placed finish would send the Olyroos into a playoff match against an African nation.
Vidmar said he couldn’t pick any players who were set to be ineligible for the Asian Cup in April as he felt for those missing “on a personal level”.
“Unfortunately, the Asian Cup falls outside of a designated FIFA window, which presents challenges in players seeking releases from their respective clubs to join us in Qatar,” he said.
“It’s certainly disappointing not to have access to all those who are eligible for the Asian Cup, and on a personal level, I feel for those players who won’t have the opportunity to experience the tournament and reap the benefits in terms of their continued development.
“It was something we always knew would be a possibility, so there has been a lot of planning that has gone into our preparation over the last 12 months, built on the understanding of the circumstances we could face regarding Asian Cup selection.”
Teenage Socceroos prodigy Garang Kuol was named in the squad despite struggling for minutes at his Dutch loan club Volendam and is set to reunite with his older brother Alou in attack at the West Asian championships.
But Melbourne City star Marco Tilio’s hopes of playing at either tournament have been shattered by a hamstring tendon injury that City confirmed on Friday.
The 22-year-old winger, who is on loan from Celtic and has seven Socceroos caps, will be sidelined for up to six weeks.
Despite his injury there was no room in the squad for Adelaide United teen star and future Bayern Munich player Nestory Irankunda.

title: Women’s World Cup 2023: How Australia must capitalise on $1.32 billion success of home tournament
subtitle: The FIFA Women’s World Cup set a new benchmark for sport in Australia but Football Australia CEO James Johnson said it’s just the beginning.
content:
The FIFA Women’s World Cup set a benchmark for female sport in this country but Football Australia CEO James Johnson 
The World Cup had a huge impact and the economic benefit to Australia has been tallied at $1.32 billion. 
. Sales of their jersey were up 19 per cent on the 2019 edition, viewership numbers broke records and every match they played was a sellout. 
However, building the Matildas’ profile wasn’t Football Australia’s only mission during the World Cup.
Johnson wanted to create a legacy similar to the one achieved by the Sydney 2000 Olympics. 
The report, due to be released on Friday, reveals just how big an impact the tournament had and the 
Club memberships increased by 669 per cent in 2023 from the previous year.
More than 27,000 children registered for Liberty A-League passes, well up on the 8800 from 2022. 
More fans than ever before are watching the games. The average attendance is 2500, up from 1240 from last year, and streaming of the matches has reportedly increased by 120 per cent.
At a grassroots level, participation has soared, particularly in schools, while the participation of women and girls has increased from 21 per cent in 2021 to 26 per cent.
Despite the huge success, Johnson said the job was far from done.
“To continue this trajectory we aim to secure the hosting rights for the AFC Women’s Asian Cup 2026, which will require government support at all levels,” he said.
“We believe that this will once again be a huge value generator for Australia and another boost to the ongoing growth of Australian football, and more broadly throughout Asia and the Oceania region.
“These successes have seen a dramatic increase in women’s participation in football, which is adding more pressure on the need for government investment at all levels to closing the $2.9 billion gap in facility investment across Australia.
“With over 2400 clubs at capacity, we continue to work with all levels of government to meet the needs of 1.7 million participants across Australia.”
Football Australia head of women’s football, World Cup legacy and inclusion, Sarah Walsh, said the Matildas had shown change was possible. 
“The Matildas have been at the forefront of transformative societal change, challenging perceptions and gender stereotypes while advocating for sustained evolution within the Australian and international sporting landscape,” Walsh said. 
“The Legacy ’23 post-tournament report delves into the success achieved in leveraging the tournament.
“However, it emphasises the need for increased funding to ensure that the legacy of the FIFA Women’s World Cup isn’t merely a momentary triumph but evolves into foundations for a thriving, equitable and dynamic future for football.”
In the same way the Olympics benefited multiple sports, the Women’s World Cup legacy is not limited to football. 
Federal and state governments invested $398 million into the Legacy ’23 program and related initiatives.
A total of $269 million was channelled into advancing football but 33 per cent of the funds have benefited other sports. 
Millions were spent upgrading the stadiums used during the tournament, including their change rooms, lighting, a sensory room at Suncorp Stadium, improved media facilities, bigger screens, player recovery areas, new turnstiles and pitch upgrades.
These improvements will have huge benefits for the National Rugby League and rugby union. 
Major upgrades were also completed at community clubs used by international teams to train during the World Cup. They are a huge benefit to grassroots clubs and players. 
The huge rise in participation means many community clubs are now bursting at the seams.
Johnson said the success of the tournament and the legacy proved more investment was needed.
“As we aim to host the AFC Women’s Asian Cup 2026 and bid for the 2020 FIFA World Club Cup to contribute to the growth of Asian football, we are committed to ensuring that the legacy of the FIFA Women’s World Cup continues to thrive, benefiting not just football but the wider Australian society,” he said. 
Originally published as

title: Former Sydney FC midfielder Patrick Yazbek poised to make his Socceroos debut
subtitle: Patrick Yazbek’s decision to choose the Socceroos over Lebanon hasn’t gone down well with the Cedars as he is poised to make his international debut against the country he snubbed.
content:
Likely Socceroos debutant Patrick Yazbek’s decision to pledge his international allegiance to Australia rather than Lebanon has been questioned by Cedars coach Miodrag Radulovic.
Socceroos coach Graham Arnold said that former Sydney FC midfielder Yazbek was a “more than 90 per cent” chance to make his national team debut against Lebanon in Tuesday night’s 
“He’s Australian first and foremost,” Arnold said of the Sydney-born, Norway-based Yazbek, whose heritage is Lebanese.
“Him mum and dad are from Lebanon, and he’s got that in him as well … he’s a fantastic kid.
“(To) make his debut against Lebanon, it’s a great thing for him and his family that they’ll never forget.”
However, Radulovic said 21-year-old Yazbek would have been better off playing for Lebanon.
“I think it would be better to be one of the leaders in our team than sitting on the bench (for Australia), but this is his decision,” the Montenegro-born mentor said.
“I’m not interested anymore.”
The Lebanese squad does include one player born in Australia, former Central Coast Mariners Academy attacker Jackson Khoury.
“He has big potential. He’s the future of the Lebanese team,” Radulovic said of the 21-year-old Khoury.
Radulovic was “optimistic” about Lebanon’s chances in Canberra, saying his side’s performance in last Thursday’s loss to the Socceroos in Sydney was “much better” than the 2-0 scoreline indicated.
“We will try to correct the mistakes that we did, and to be much more effective in attack. I expect a good performance and a much better result,” he said.
Radulovic said he was using the games against the Socceroos to prepare for June’s World Cup qualifiers against Palestine and Bangladesh.
“We need to win those games in June, that’s our target,” said Radulovic, with Lebanon a huge chance to progress to the next round of AFC World Cup qualifiers with success against Palestine and Bangladesh.
The Socceroos – whose starting side could have up to five changes from last week – will guarantee themselves a berth in the next round of qualifiers with a win in Canberra.
However, Arnold is desperate to win not only on Tuesday night but in June, also against Palestine and Bangladesh, to ensure the Socceroos have a perfect AFC second-round qualifying record, which should result in them being one of the three nations in pot one for the third-round qualifying draw.
“What’s important is we win these three games,” Arnold said.
“My focus is the players and getting the job done for the nation.
“It’s important that we go out there with the focus and the mentality, and most of all the energy in front of a full house to put on a great performance.”
Tuesday, 7.45pm (AEDT)
GIO Stadium, Canberra
TV: Network 10

title: Socceroos coach Graham Arnold unhappy with tackle that left playmaker Ajdin Hrustic in tears
subtitle: The Socceroos’ easy win of Lebanon was marred by an ankle injury suffered by playmaker Ajdin Hrustic.
content:
Socceroos coach Graham Arnold says Lebanese midfielder Ali Tneich should have been sent off for his “horrible” tackle on Ajdin Hrustic that left the playmaker in tears as he was helped off the field with an ankle injury in Canberra on Tuesday night.
Hrustic’s injury was the low point of an otherwise impressive night for the Socceroos, who thrashed the Cedars 5-0 at GIO Stadium.
Attacking weapon Craig Goodwin was superb in scoring a brace, while strikers Kusini Yengi and John Iredale each netted their first goal for the Socceroos as Australia sealed its spot in the next of round of AFC qualifiers for the 2026 World Cup.
However, Hrustic’s injury somewhat marred the occasion.
Having come off the bench in last week’s 2-0 win over Lebanon after missing the Socceroos’ previous 11 matches because of a lack of football at club level, Hrustic was a starter on Tuesday night, with his creative skills evident in his assist for Goodwin’s first goal of night in the 48th minute.
But soon after, he was left reeling after falling victim to a studs-up tackle from Tneich that caught the inside of his ankle.
Arnold consoled a teary Hrustic as he was assisted from the ground and replaced by debutant Patrick Yazbek.
Tneich was only shown a yellow card for the tackle, but had the VAR system in operation, Arnold was adamant the punishment would have been upgraded to a send off.
“I will say if there was VAR that was (a) red (card),” the Socceroos coach said.
“It was a pretty horrible tackle when you look at it back.”
In terms of the severity of the injury, Arnold said it was a “good sign” that Hrustic was “hobbling around” in the dressing-room.
Wearing a moon boot, Hrustic was able to fly back to the Netherlands in the early hours of Wednesday morning to link with his club Heracles, who will organise scans for the 27-year-old midfielder.
Goodwin was hopeful Hrustic’s injury wasn’t “too bad”.
“It’s really disappointing for him to come off with that injury,” the man-of-the-match said.
“I don’t particularly think that they were trying to kick people or make things aggressive, but that is something that we encounter on a regular basis in these qualifiers.
“Teams will try to put that physical presence on us because we are one of the top teams in Asia, and it you give us too much time then we can punish you.”
“It was a really good night for myself and for us as a team to put in a decent performance and contribute to a lot of goals,” the former Adelaide United captain said.
“When these (international) windows come up I want to be involved in every single game and play as much as I can. so to miss that one (last Thursday) was a little bit hard to take, but I was really happy I could make up for it tonight.”
.

Having come off the bench in last week’s 2-0 win over Lebanon after missing the Socceroos’ previous 11 matches because of a lack of football at club level, Hrustic was a starter on Tuesday night, with his creative skills evident in his assist for Goodwin’s first goal of night in the 48th minute.
But soon after, he was left reeling after falling victim to a studs-up tackle from Tneich that caught the inside of his ankle.
Arnold consoled a teary Hrustic as he was assisted from the ground and replaced by debutant Patrick Yazbek.
Tneich was only shown a yellow card for the tackle, but had the VAR system in operation, Arnold was adamant the punishment would have been upgraded to a send off.
“I will say if there was VAR that was (a) red (card),” the Socceroos coach said.
“It was a pretty horrible tackle when you look at it back.”
In terms of the severity of the injury, Arnold said it was a “good sign” that Hrustic was “hobbling around” in the dressing-room.
Wearing a moon boot, Hrustic was able to fly back to the Netherlands in the early hours of Wednesday morning to link with his club Heracles, who will organise scans for the 27-year-old midfielder.
Goodwin was hopeful Hrustic’s injury wasn’t “too bad”.
“It’s really disappointing for him to come off with that injury,” the man-of-the-match said.
“I don’t particularly think that they were trying to kick people or make things aggressive, but that is something that we encounter on a regular basis in these qualifiers.
“Teams will try to put that physical presence on us because we are one of the top teams in Asia, and it you give us too much time then we can punish you.”
“It was a really good night for myself and for us as a team to put in a decent performance and contribute to a lot of goals,” the former Adelaide United captain said.
“When these (international) windows come up I want to be involved in every single game and play as much as I can. so to miss that one (last Thursday) was a little bit hard to take, but I was really happy I could make up for it tonight.”
.
en_subtitle: The Socceroos’ easy win of Lebanon was marred by an ankle injury suffered by playmaker Ajdin Hrustic.

title: Socceroos hammer Lebanon in World Cup qualifier as record falls
subtitle: It was the Craig Goodwin show in Canberra with the Socceroos ace helping Australia into the next stage of World Cup qualification.
content:
Australia cruised into the next stage of Asian qualifying for the 2026 World Cup with a 5-0 drubbing of Lebanon in Canberra on Tuesday.
Craig Goodwin’s two goals, plus strikes from Kusini Yengi, John Iredale and a Bassel Jradi own goal gave Australia a maximum 12 points after four games and they are now assured of progressing from Group I.
It was the Craig Goodwin show in front of a record GIO Stadium crowd of 25,023, the largest for a football match in Canberra. 
“When I knew Craig Goodwin younger, he didn’t believe in himself like he does these days,” Australia coach Graham Arnold said of the 32-year-old. 
“He’s a top-quality player, but he’s a fantastic person and a great leader. “His delivery, set pieces, is fantastic and his finishing, it’s just got better and better as he gets older.”
It took just two minutes for Goodwin to have an impact on his return to the side after illness when his teasing cross found Yengi to open his international account.
Yengi, a striker who plays for Portsmouth in the English third tier, bundled home at the second time of asking after his initial effort hit the post.
Goodwin almost made a second with another pinpoint delivery after 43 minutes but Harry Souttar’s header struck the woodwork and it remained 1-0 at half-time.
As in the first half, Lebanon conceded after two minutes and again Goodwin, who plays for Al Wehda in Saudi Arabia, was the creator.
His free-kick from the right was headed goalwards by Souttar where ‘keeper Mostafa Matar’s save hit hapless teammate Jradi and ricocheted back into the net.
A minute later Goodwin got his reward for a dominant display when lashing home left-footed superbly from just outside the box to make it 3-0.
Substitute John Iredale tapped in the fourth with his first touch after 68 minutes and Goodwin bagged his second from close range with nine minutes to go to cap a fine personal display.

title: New Roo Patrick Yazbek never had any intention of playing for Lebanon
subtitle: Patrick Yazbek is proud of his Lebanese heritage but representing Australia was always his priority.
content:
Despite his Lebanese heritage, Patrick Yazbek has only ever wanted to play for the Socceroos.
And having rejected the Cedars’ advances, the former Sydney FC midfielder’s dream came true when he made his debut for Australia’s senior national team, coming on as a substitute in his side’s 5-0 thrashing of Lebanon in Tuesday night’s AFC second-round World Cup qualifier in Canberra.
“I was born and raised in Australia,” the proud Yazbek said.
“I do have that Lebanese heritage from my dad in particular who was born there, and my mum with Lebanese parents but who was born in Australia, but for me I’ve always wanted to be a Socceroo.
“I’ve had all the photos in my room ever since I’ve been young. It’s just a dream come true.
“It’s an honour to represent Australia.”
Before the match, Lebanon coach Miodrag Radulovic questioned why Yazbek would want to sit on the bench for Australia when he could be a “leader” with the Cedars.
“That’s just his opinion. He’s got to look after his team, so he’s entitled to say what he wants,” Yazbek said.
“I know that playing for Australia has been my dream since I first kicked a ball.
“It’s such a privilege to be Australian because we have so much opportunity here and it’s something that I don’t take for granted, (but) as much as I am an Aussie, I do have that touch with my Lebanese side and it’s just a blessing to play for Australia.”
Making the occasion more special on Tuesday was Yazbek providing an assist for John Iredale – another ex-Sky Blues youth player – to score his first goal for the Socceroos.
“I’m happy to contribute, and the main goal is to keep contributing,” said Yazbek, who joined Norwegian club Viking in February last year.
“That’s also performing at club land, but I just want to be involved here as much as I can.
“It’s something that I definitely will remember forever.”
As will Iredale, who became teary after scoring in just his second Socceroos appearance.
“It means the world to me – I’ve been dreaming of that moment,” the 24-year-old Germany-based marksman said.
“I dedicate that goal to two very special people in my life, my fiancee, it’s her birthday … and to my Pop. He missed the last game (last Thursday’s 2-0 win over Lebanon) because he was in hospital, (but) he fought hard and got himself home to watch this game from the lounge. so I’m very happy to get that goal.”

title: Injured Socceroos midfielder Riley McGree to miss rest of 2023-24 campaign
subtitle: There has been mixed news on the injury front for three Socceroos players following last month’s two wins over Lebanon.
content:
Socceroos star Riley McGree will miss Australia’s June World Cup qualifiers against Bangladesh and Palestine after being ruled out for the rest of the season with a foot injury.
McGree suffered the injury in the Socceroos’ 2-0 win over Lebanon at Sydney’s CommBank Stadium on March 21.
The 25-year-old attacking midfielder didn’t play when the teams met again in Canberra last Tuesday, instead leaving Australia’s camp early to return to his English Championship club Middlesbrough.
Boro coach Michael Carrick has subsequently announced that McGree requires surgery and will be sidelined for the remainder of the 2023-24 campaign.
“Riley needs an operation and is out for the season,” Carrick said.
McGree was one of three Socceroos players injured across the two games against Lebanon.
Belgium-based Jordy Bos, who hurt his knee after coming on as a substitute for McGree, is expected to be sidelined for six weeks.
However, it was better news for playmaker Ajdin Hrustic, who was forced off in Australia’s 5-0 win in Canberra after copping a nasty kick to the inside of his ankle.
Hrustic returned to the Netherlands in a moon boot but was able to start for his club team Heracles in their weekend 1-0 loss to FC Twente.
The 27-year-old Dandenong product played 84 minutes of the contest before being replaced.
Regardless of the results of June’s matches against Bangladesh and Palestine, the Socceroos have already guaranteed themselves a spot in the Asian Football Confederation’s third round of World Cup qualifiers.
However, Socceroos coach Graham Arnold is intent on his side winning both games to give Australia the best possible chance of being placed in pot one for the third-round draw.

title: ‘Painful’: Ange Postecoglou in icy exchange after Tottenham nightmare
subtitle: Ange Postecoglou was visibly unhappy after a nightmare unfolded in one of his Tottenham club’s biggest games of the season.
content:
Ange Postecoglou was not in the mood for it as he faced the press following his Tottenham club’s nightmare derby loss to bitter rivals Arsenal. 
The Australian manager admitted he was frustrated with his players as Spurs slumped to a second consecutive defeat that leaves the club’s quest to play in the Champions League hanging by a thread. 
Arsenal’s tense 3-2 win at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium saw them retain their spot on the top of the table, surviving the nervous dying minutes as Tottenham launched a late comeback. 
Mikel Arteta’s side stormed into a three-goal lead in the first half, before Tottenham scored two second half goals to make it a grandstand finish.
It was all set up by a 23-minute first half blitz that put Arsenal up 3-0. 
Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg’s own goal put Arsenal ahead early before Bukayo Saka fired home and Kai Havertz headed in from virtually on the goalline to put Arsenal in command.
Cristian Romero’s goal gave Tottenham hope as he punished a wayward pass by Arsenal keeper David Raya, before Son Heung-min’s 87th-minute penalty, conceded by Declan Rice’s needless foul on Ben Davies, set up an anxious finale.
They survived by their finger tips to become the first Arsenal side to win league games at Tottenham in successive seasons since the late 1980s.
With fourth-placed Aston Villa seven points clear of fifth-placed Tottenham, Postecoglou’s side must win their two games in hand to have any chance of staying in the race for Champions League qualification.
“Disappointing day for us. We didn’t get the outcome we wanted from a big game,” he said.
“There are a lot of moments in games when we don’t sense that you are giving good opposition time and space to do things. They are going to hurt you.
“I don’t think it’s about just set-pieces. We were very poor on those but there is a lot more to fix.”
He was much more terse with reporters during his press conference, which didn’t last long, 
“From our perspective, we allowed them way too easy access to our goal. They got there three or four times and scored three goals in the first half. It’s not acceptable at this level and we paid a price for it against a very good team,” he said.
“We showed resilience and fought back but we had to because there was no other choice. We couldn’t come out in the second half and not give our supporters a little bit of hope.
“We’re still not as resilient as we can be, particularly in those kinds of moments [in the first half] where there are transitions or set-pieces.”
Spurs captain Son Heung-min also admitted it was a “painful” day.
“We could have come back after 3-2. I think we had a good chance and a good opportunity,” he said.
“Especially in those games if you concede goals like that it’s difficult and painful.
“They were clinical and strong in the air. We had a lot of opportunities, hitting the post and having a disallowed goal.
“As I said before when you concede goals like this you have to be strong.”
Arteta, meanwhile, believes the Gunners are capable of winning the league, holding a one point lead over Manchester City, who have one game in hand. 
Asked if Arsenal, chasing a first title since 2004, had shown they were equipped to be champions, Arteta said: “I think so. 100 per cent. I have seen that every day since the start of the season.
“What is ahead is beautiful. The margins are so small. Obviously we expect to have a real go.
“Don’t get carried away with yourself. We want to be better. There are margins for improvement. Go again against Bournemouth next weekend because it’s going to be really tough.” 
Arteta was impressed with the way his players responded to their self-inflicted wounds and kept Tottenham at bay in the pressure-packed final minutes.
“When you are at the highest competitive level it is not always going to go for you. It is how you react. How much do they want it? It is part of the journey,” he said.
“3-0 up you are in control and dominating. Then something clicks in your brain, we made a mistake, they scored and it’s game on.
“I have a lot of faith in the players but I was doubting a bit in the last few minutes. We had to dig in.
“We have done it two years in a row here which is extremely difficult. We had to suffer in the second half. Great. It’s good learning. Something you can grab in the future.” Arteta singled out Havertz for praise after the often-criticised German played through illness to deliver an influential display, featuring a superb long pass that set up Saka’s goal prior to his own clinical header.
“He was sensational in every department today. He wasn’t 100 percent. He was ill before the match,” Arteta said.
— with AFP

“3-0 up you are in control and dominating. Then something clicks in your brain, we made a mistake, they scored and it’s game on.
“I have a lot of faith in the players but I was doubting a bit in the last few minutes. We had to dig in.
“We have done it two years in a row here which is extremely difficult. We had to suffer in the second half. Great. It’s good learning. Something you can grab in the future.” Arteta singled out Havertz for praise after the often-criticised German played through illness to deliver an influential display, featuring a superb long pass that set up Saka’s goal prior to his own clinical header.
“He was sensational in every department today. He wasn’t 100 percent. He was ill before the match,” Arteta said.

title: Australian Arsenal fan goes viral after Tottenham EPL ticket fail
subtitle: This young Aussie is lucky English football hooliganism is just about a thing of the past after his epic Premier League ticket fail.
content:
The English Premier League famously features some of the fiercest rivalries and most loyal fanbases in all of sport.
While the days of intense violence in and out of stadiums that once plagued the sport has thankfully just about been stamped out of the game, hatred among some fans remains as strong as ever.
One of the most heated clashes in football is the North London Derby between Arsenal and Tottenham, a match-up that has been going for well over a century.
The latest instalment was held on Sunday night Australian time at Tottenham Stadium between a title-chasing Gunners team and a Spurs side still in with a shot of a top-four finish.
In an entertaining clash, Arsenal took a 3-0 lead into halftime and then withstood a Spurs comeback for a 3-2 victory.
This is where a young Aussie comes in, a bloke being called the “bravest Arsenal fan in the world”.
The as-yet unnamed Australian from Sydney decided to book a last-minute ticket to fly to London and watch his beloved Gunners in the massive game.
Most of his family is from London and they are all huge Arsenal fans.
The only issue? The ticket he booked was to sit among the Tottenham fans, a massive footballing faux pas.
The story became known to AFTV Media, an Arsenal supporter group that has over 3.5 million followers across YouTube, Instagram and X.
“We had a brave performance today and I’m standing next to one of the bravest men in the crowd,” an AFTV host said on a video from outside the stadium.
“I looked up and saw you undoing your jacket with the Arsenal top amongst the Spurs fans.
“What happened?”
See there is an added twist to the story that goes beyond simply buying the wrong ticket.
“I just got off a plane last night, from Sydney Australia,” the fan begins in the video you can see above.
“I come straight to Tottenham Stadium. I bought my ticket in Sydney (and) I didn’t realise I was in the Tottenham section.
“Obviously we win 3-2, I go up to the barrier, and I see all the Arsenal fans.
“I couldn’t help myself, I honestly couldn’t help myself.”
The act he couldn’t help was opening the blue and grey jacket he was wearing to proudly display his bright red Arsenal shirt underneath.
High up in the stands, surrounded by Spurs supporters, he then raises his right arm and pumps his fist in celebration towards the Gunners fan section.
As the camera pans away, you can see Spurs fans pointing in his direction.
The young lad did well to get out of the stadium fully intact.
In years gone by, this likely would not have had a happy ending.
But he could smile and tell his story in a video that’s been viewed 157,000 times on X, with 2,500 comments and over 300 retweets.
It also has over 22,000 likes on Instagram and more than 21,000 views on YouTube.
Most of the comments came from Arsenal fans praising the young Aussie.
“Shout out to our brother from Australia … kept it real and undercover,” was one comment.
“This is mad brave, how do you do this?” asked another.
“Hero. And to be fair, that was brave. Lucky not to get a slap. Legend,” added a third.
“That’s one thing I like about the Aussies, they just don’t give two hoots,” wrote another.
“What a legend,” posted another. “Thank God he survived.”
